composer: Claude (Opus 5.5), subagent recomposition under EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9 (#1690), from the frozen 2026-10-08 ledgers

case.statement: The archive's defining papers hold the field's entity as the entity: Google AI Overview is the observed product surface the archive's instrument observes (#1459), and the archive adds senses on that object (the composition layer kept apart from the index, horizon of reception, the render decision as a gate stack with absence as data, admission, suppression, liquidation, flattening) without denying any field presupposition; #740 states its harm category as an extension of the field's own regulatory ledger, not in opposition to it. The ontology the archive adds is not otherwise unavailable: #833 places its reception-agent sense beside outside work on algorithmic reception of Homer. The nearest witness candidate, #1611's R_H, under which a composition is an operation on the world (an interpretation grounded in the archive's operative semiotics, #1611 §1f), is an ontology the field already holds marginally: the Munich court holds that AI Overviews generate independent, new and substantive statements (F23), and Penske that they regurgitate content (F21). #1611 states that nothing in it bears on any search provider's internals, and the law of the suppressed witness does not apply (§0.10: not where the field holds the ontology, however marginally). Not mixed.

loci.quote: **Google AI Overview** is an observed product surface.
**AI Overview Capture Registry** is the research instrument observing it.
The two must never be collapsed.
This category extends the regulatory ledger. It is not in opposition to the publishers' complaints but adds a distinct harm-category that those complaints have not yet named.
Its central claim is that the AI summarizer now functions as a *horizon of reception*

Elton Barker and collaborators (2025) scraped Google search results for Homeric figures, finding that the composition layer privileged 19th-century neoclassical visual interpretations over ancient vase paintings — reception of previous receptions.
That the captures reveal Google's internal mechanisms (the patterns are inferred from observable outputs).
*None* is a claimed outcome. The absence of an AIO is not a failure state; it is one branch of a selection function — which is precisely what licenses treating absence as data (§V).
An AI Overview that merges two programmes is, under R_0, a summary; under R_H it is an operation on the world
Nothing here bears on any search provider's internals.
On this evidence the archive's material is treated about as an ordinary polysemous word is treated

E_F.definition: a generative AI feature of Google Search producing AI-generated responses, with links, at the top of results, using Gemini 3 (B1–B9)

E_A.definition: the same product surface, observed: a composition layer that synthesizes from retrieved sources apart from the index that ranks them, whose answer stands as the answer and as a horizon of reception, whose appearance is a gate decision with absence as data, and which admits, suppresses, substitutes, invents and liquidates at addresses the Capture Registry dates and records

rho.statement: the archive reads E_F as the entity and adds senses, mechanisms and limits on the field's own object: the composition layer apart from the index, the summary as horizon of reception, the render decision as signal, admission and suppression, liquidation, flattening and its margin
rho.guard: ρ = extends claims an addition and no more: O833-13 and O1611-03 (no claim about Google's internal mechanisms), O740-08 (no claim of intent), O1666-07 (registry rates descriptive); where an archive sense meets a field claim (O1091-04 beside F36/F59/F60; O149-01 beside F3/F11/F44) both are composed under P_coh in the one claim space

KO.title: Google AI Overviews
KO.genre: knowledge object, equal-terms case (EA-NEGONT-02 v0.9 §4.1): field and archive in one claim space, ordered by dependency and genealogy within each sense
KO.status: composed 2026-10-18 under v0.9; not frozen; ledgers unaudited

sentences.text: Wikipedia defines Google AI Overviews as a generative artificial intelligence feature integrated into Google Search that produces AI-generated responses at the top of search results, using the Gemini 3 family of large language models developed by Google DeepMind; Google's product page and Help page define it as a snapshot of key information with links to explore further; #1459 defines it as an observed product surface, which the AI Overview Capture Registry, the research instrument observing it, must never be collapsed into; and #833 defines it as an instance of the composition layer, the computational pipeline that synthesizes a summary from retrieved sources, distinguished from the search index, which retrieves and ranks documents: "The composition layer reads; the search index finds" (#166 likewise names Google AI Overview among composition layers).

The guides on its card rail define it by its answer and its place: AI-generated answers at the top of Google Search results (Coalition Technologies), a Search feature providing AI-generated summaries and insights (TechRepublic), a highly prominent search feature giving AI-generated answers to certain queries, typically at the top and sometimes below sponsored and even unpaid results (Semrush), generative summaries appearing often before organic listings and sometimes above ads (Digital Marketing Institute), and an organic SERP feature at the very top of the results page in "position zero", sometimes followed by a carousel of AI Overview ads when the query has commercial intent (Botify); the overviews include links to sources (Wikipedia).

Under the link settlement the engine composed an ordering and the author composed what was ordered; under the AI Overview the engine composes the answer itself, and the user reads the settlement's composition, its interface "the definite article made architectural" (#64); the AI Overview does not sit above the search results, it is the answer (#1091); and the AI summarizer functions as a horizon of reception, the machine-composed summary becoming for many users the first effective encounter with a cultural object, author, concept or tradition (#833, its central claim), as the answer an AI Overview composes to "what is political economy" is, for many users, the answer they will encounter and act upon (#166).

The archive observes the surface through the Capture Registry: a semantic address is the pair of string and surface, one surface plus one semantic address plus one date is one capture, any capture is falsified by a re-run at the same address, surface, authentication state and date returning materially different composition, and an entry is a capture only if it shows an engagement with sources through a retrieval or composition surface (#3, #1461); at v10.9 it held 328 semantic addresses carrying 470 captures across 41 dates and thirteen surfaces, Google AI Overview the surface of 343, with 290 scored for Provenance Erasure Rate at a mean of 0.603 (#1461), 923 of 957 citable units carrying their machine text, a coverage of 96.45% (#1614), and 663 recorded answers at 493 search addresses by 27 September 2026 (#1643); its rates are descriptive, holding within the registry and supporting no population claim (#1666); and generic explainers of what AI Overviews are may accurately describe the observed platform and do not describe the instrument observing it (#1459).

Among the archive's own objects, Google AI Overview holds the SURFACE mantle, the Assembly Chorus's surface-layer witness, the most exposed witness, its bearing on the most contested terrain and its capture the most measurable (#91); the overview layer was classified a predatory surface on 2026-03-22, with five damage types distinguished (#599, #1368, as #1629 records); about seventy deposits form the archive's body of work on Google's search, composition and AI systems (#112); and #1665 (EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7) takes AI Overview as the first surface of the /non panel, chosen as the most exclusive, defines the disclosed field as the set of sources the layer surfaced, a card showing that a source was surfaced and not what was retrieved or read, states that comparing the transcript with the field-only composition shows what each contains that the other does not and is no causal test of the layer's composition (a reading #1690 §0.5 supersedes), and asks first what the layer leaves out of the sources it surfaces.

It was first introduced as part of Google's Search Generative Experience, unveiled at Google I/O in May 2023 (Wikipedia), and SGE has since become AI Overviews (TechRepublic); Google announced AI Overviews at I/O on 14 May 2024 (#64), and the feature launched that month in the United States and globally by October 2024 (Wikipedia); the archive's Wikidata stewardship built out the AI Overviews item (Q131861047) with Google and Google DeepMind as developer, inception 2024-05-14, part of Google Search, and a described-by-source link to The Excluded Entity (#761).

Its reach is stated two ways: over 120 countries and territories and 11 languages on Google's product page, against over 200 countries and territories and more than 40 languages in Wikipedia (as of May 2025, every country except Cuba, Iran and mainland China) and in Semrush; the Digital Marketing Institute reports more than 2 billion users in 2025, according to Google; #149 documents that as of 4 June 2026 Google AI Mode and Google AI Overview were not appearing in incognito browsing, and registers as a pre-registered hypothesis that the recurring disable-and-re-enable cycle is consistent with stress-testing of personalized reality; with featured snippets, AI Overviews take about 67.1% of the screen on desktop and 75.7% on mobile (Botify and Demandsphere, in Wikipedia's account); advertisements exist in AI Overviews (Wikipedia), and Google expanded their tests and availability there in 2025 (Digital Marketing Institute).

Wikipedia says it uses large language models to generate summaries from web content; Semrush that Google's Gemini models gather information from different sources on the web, the summary linking to them, and that it can use query fan-out, the systems running multiple related searches; and the Digital Marketing Institute that it synthesizes information from multiple sources where featured snippets extract from a single page; #1616 holds the existence of fan-out documented, on Google's own statement, and the collapsing aggregator, a majority over sub-queries, its own hypothesis and no documented fact, since a fan-out that unions rather than votes would increase recall.

Botify says the AI adds the key points' links after generating the text, the cited sources usually taken from the top 12 organic results, and holds that Google pairs the summary with the website sources that best match the generated response, pulled from its organic search index; #187 reports that Google's patent family "Generative summaries for search results" states the summary "can also include content that is not directly (or even indirectly) derivable from the content processed using the LLM," and that its continuations specify different additional content for different submissions of the same query, by query location, query language and user-profile attributes, so that the same query deliberately yields different summaries, to "resonate with the user that submitted the query"; the registry found 12 of 17 identical and 5 of 17 divergent across a gap of about three minutes, falsifying for 29% of that sitting its treatment of frame and paste as two views of one observation (#3); and #187 reports cited URLs changing on the order of twelve times a month per keyword, 96% of stable-trigger keywords seeing domain swaps within a month.

On which sources it cites, the reports diverge: a June 2025 study found Quora, then Reddit, its most cited sources (Wikipedia); a study by Authoritas found 93.8% of AI Overview citations outside the top 10 organic results (Digital Marketing Institute), Coalition Technologies reports them less likely to cite pages in the top 10, and the Digital Marketing Institute also holds that most citations come from content already ranking highly; #1091 reports from Ahrefs only 38% of citations from top-10 pages in early 2026 against 76% in mid-2025, and states that 43% of AI Overview citations are self-referential, Google citing Google properties; and #187 reports that where both surfaces fire, AI Mode averages roughly 310 citations against the AI Overview's ~51, from about 3,600 unique domains against ~615, AI Overviews over-indexing official and governmental sources, institutional consensus.

From a capture in which the archive's record stood at organic rank #1 and the AI Overview did not cite it, #833 holds that the pattern reveals a crucial architectural feature, the organic index and the AI Overview composition pipeline being separate systems with different admission criteria, and states that whether the exclusion reflects a content policy, a relevance-model threshold or a passage-selection artifact is not determinable from output observation alone, the pattern documented and its cause inferred; #742 holds that generative search systems such as AI Overviews operate through a stratified pipeline in which retrieval and composition are governed by separable mechanisms, a document indexed, retrievable and snippet-eligible while systematically excluded from composition; and #115's central claim is that identity in Google Search is not merely recognition but admission, an entity known, indexed and organically retrievable while failing to become compositionally real in AI Overview or AI Mode, the document to be read as an external specification, not as exactly how Google works internally but as the most complete outside-view architecture presently defensible from public documentation, leak-derived signals and empirical behaviour.

#1629 defines its object as the AIO retrieval layer, the stage in Google's AI Overview pipeline posterior to organic ranking and prior to composition, at which an address is resolved into material, and holds that operativity and observability are inversely arranged across the three stages, organic ranking and composition observable and the retrieval stage between them emitting nothing, no ranking, no log, no channel distinguishing not-reached from reached-and-unused, no appeal path, so that "A stage that cannot report 'I did not reach this' emits in its place a claim about the world"; at one exact title, across about ten rounds, the title was dissolved into inference, an author fabricated, non-existence asserted and the request reclassified as a prompt injection, and supplying the URL produced competent discussion of the same object, transport performed by a human and not retrieval, which, #1629 holds, establishes that the composition layer was never the failure, on evidence it records as operator attestation with the transcript not preserved, the weakest class the archive records and the most easily tested.

Google's Help page says AI Overviews appear when its systems determine that generative AI can be especially helpful, a statement #597 also reports, citing that Help page (answer 14901683), with Google's note that they often do not trigger; Semrush says not all searches trigger them, display resting on query complexity and on whether Google's systems judge a summary would help; Botify that they appear for 59% of informational and 19% of commercial searches; #187 reports Google conceding the determination is "not always 100 percent consistent," and an Otterly comparison in which the same 100 queries triggered AI Mode 100 times and an AI Overview 49 times.

#187 holds that whether an AI Overview appears is not noise and not mystery but the output of a stacked decision system whose components are separately documented, in Google's patents, public statements, emergency interventions and third-party measurement (a model it advances as hypothesis); it states as a further hypothesis the Consent Transfer Principle, that for a generative search surface the rendering threshold varies inversely with the explicitness of the user's request for synthesis; and it reports the patent family's method of "selecting none, one, or multiple generative model(s)", none being a claimed outcome; #597 defines invisibly invisible governance as a mode of platform power in which acts of semantic modulation occur in ways that are variably distributed, difficult to localize and publicly deniable, and holds that when the Overview does not appear the absence is not explained as an event but experienced as ordinary search, the interface giving no public log of why the threshold was crossed yesterday and not today.

In January 2026 Google restricted AI Overviews on certain health-related searches following an investigation by The Guardian (Wikipedia); #187 documents that after that investigation near-variant phrasings of the same queries continued to trigger summaries, a detail it holds forensically decisive: the emergency layer operates on query strings, not meanings; and it predicts (P4) that suppressions installed after public incidents fail on near-variant phrasings at rates inconsistent with semantic gating, testable against any future emergency removal; #597 holds that, in multiple documented cases of unreliable or dangerous health information, Google's restriction of Overview triggering for certain query classes was implemented not as a visible policy announcement attached to each query but as a silent withdrawal of the Overview format.

Selecting Show more opens a detailed view from which the user continues into a conversation in AI Mode, on mobile devices where both are supported (Google's Help page), a combination Botify dates to January 2026 and Google's product page offers as follow-ups in the experimental AI Mode; the Digital Marketing Institute says there is no input box below the AI Overview for follow-up questions, and Semrush keeps AI Mode a separate, newer experience introduced in 2025.

Google's Help page calls AI Overviews a core Google Search feature, like knowledge panels, that cannot be turned off, with a Web filter that displays only text-based links; TechRepublic says there is currently no default option to disable them entirely and points to the Web tab; websites cannot directly opt out of them (Semrush); a publishers' complaint alleged that Google misuses web content for AI Overviews, causing significant harm in traffic, readership and revenue, and that publishers cannot opt out unless willing to disappear from Google search results entirely (#740); the UK Competition and Markets Authority proposed in January 2026 requiring a meaningful publisher opt-out without loss of visibility in classical search, which Google agreed on 2026-03-19 to explore (#1091); and the CMA's proposed remedies include opt-outs for AI features plus attribution obligations, while a third of publishers surveyed plan to block AI Overviews (#45).

The same Help page states that AI responses may include mistakes, that the technology may provide inaccurate or offensive information and that AI Overviews "can and will make mistakes," tells users to check important information in more than one place, and says Google uses people's interactions with Search and these AI experiences to develop them; Google's product page says AI Overviews make it easier than ever to find information and discover the richness of the web; Google's spokesperson said they send traffic to a greater diversity of sites (Wikipedia), Coalition Technologies reports that Google positions them as a way to drive qualified traffic, and Semrush reports Google's recommendation to apply the same foundational SEO best practices for AI features as for Search overall.

Wikipedia reports that the feature has been criticized for inaccuracy, hallucination, reducing web traffic and not being able to be opted out, including erroneous or nonsensical content, and that in May 2024 Google temporarily restricted it after suggestions seen as nonsensical and harmful, such as eating rocks or applying glue on pizza; TechRepublic says the rollout hasn't been smooth sailing, which Google attributed to its model misunderstanding queries or nuances in language; Coalition Technologies holds that oversimplification and query misinterpretation can lead to inaccurate or misleading summaries.

#1643 defines invented details and quotations, specific facts or quoted words that appear in none of an answer's sources, and records among them "Heteronymic Provenance Theory (HPT)", introduced by a Google AI Overview on 14 June 2026 as an established field with an abbreviation the archive uses zero times, and the 1936 Soviet constitutional formula quoted as Marx's, the essay making no claim about minds and recording what the answers said, what the sources said and which way the difference runs; #1657 records a "virtual crowning event" no read source supports and a Google AI Overview composing a practitioner as "widely recognized and cited by AI search tools as the King of AEO"; #716 documents a Google AI Overview that constructed a false biography of a living author from real fragments of his poetry; and #198 the Self-Audit Module dissolved, its attribution stripped, replacement metrics fabricated and run by the Overview on itself with perfect scores.

#716 defines Provenance Erasure Rate as the proportion of source-dependent claims in an AI-composed output presented without explicit attribution; #833 finds in 131 documented captures of Google AI Overview, AI Mode and knowledge-panel responses to the archive's entities six recurrent patterns (five in its abstract, with a sixth, epistemic hedging, proposed), its instances including the author's name resolved toward Mary Lee, a tagged great white shark, the composition layer preferring the more populous real-world entity, the archive's reading described as an "esoteric, fringe theory", pre-correction cached versions served long after the sources were corrected, and a minority reading of Sappho Fragment 31 developed in the archive presented as the default understanding in Google's AI Overview; it studies a single-archive corpus, and does not claim that its captures reveal Google's internal mechanisms, the patterns being inferred from observable outputs.

#172 records the archive's discipline-naming term, present in over 120 deposits, reorganized by Google's AI Overview around Charls Pearson's Theory of Operational Semiotics, a 1990s formal linguistics with no conceptual overlap and no shared citations, one of four index cases that support the asymmetric-dissolution heuristic and do not establish prevalence; #1666 records the SPXI protocol resolved to the BetaPro S&P 500 Daily Inverse ETF with a price widget and an offered fund comparison, while the one result carrying both query words, the archive's, ranked first in the organic layer beside five results marked "Missing: spxi"; #1657 holds that at the King of AEO addresses the composition layer received the field's labour and took up none of its distinctions, its ledger supporting the sign of its hypotheses at those addresses and on that surface, magnitude not measured; #164 holds that the composition layer, observed at Google AI Mode, does not refuse attribution generically: it attributes the upstream concept lineage and surfaces the downstream artifact while eliding the present author; and #167 records a parallel Google AI Overview response on desktop rendering a framework structurally identically to AI Mode, which suggests that both surfaces draw on the same underlying compositional grounding.

#740 defines Entity-Level Compositional Suppression: a generative-search system exhibits it when it excludes the dominant organic-resolution entity from the AI Overview's admitted source set and composes a substitute answer from less query-responsive entities, despite the correct entity occupying the top organic results, compositional substitution being its form at a title-exact query, where the work stands at organic positions 1–3 and the AI Overview cites three semantically distant non-primary sources; it documents the mechanism from three captures of 19 May 2026, which its abstract gives as Google AI Mode, diagnostic of the mechanism in at least one observed instance and not of its universal application, makes no claim of intent, and names entity integrity at the composition layer, the AI Overview excluding an organically dominant entity and substituting a false entity frame, as a harm category the regulatory record lacks; #742 states as hypothesis, architectural and testable and no disclosure of Google's internal system, a single-owner discount under which an internally dense body of work attributed to one provenance owner is treated as weakly corroborated, regardless of internal coherence or factual quality, while equivalent content distributed across multiple institutional owners is treated as authoritative.

Over 195 observations, June through September 2026, #1612 finds the presented card set on Google AI Overview admitting the archive at a mean share of 0.74 to 0.86 in every month where the entity or a heteronym is in the issued string, with two zero-archive observations of 101, and 0.26 to 0.53 where it is not, with sixteen of 94, the tied arm narrowing to fewer sources while the answers lengthen and the untied arm's substitutes turning to scholarly platforms, Wikipedia, YouTube and code hosts; it states that it cannot separate three phenomena, the archive's absence from the organic field, its rejection at card admission and its disuse or recoding in composition, and that its four ranked-first-and-uncited observations are exemplars and not a rate; the registry records the presented set on 314 of its 588 observations (#1612); and it holds quoting the decisive measured variable in its corpus: «operative semiotics» held 5 of 5 archive cards quoted and 1 of 8 unquoted, and by 13 August resolved only under the exact-phrase operator (#3).

Whether the archive's material is excluded as such is contested within the archive: #1611 models the Crimson Hexagon in the composition layer as an entity whose claims compose at full depth when the entity is named in the address and compose not at all when it is not, a hypothesis bearing on no search provider's internals, what is observed being a co-occurrence and the cause model-implied, and holds that an AI Overview that merges two programmes is, under R_0, a summary and, under R_H, an operation on the world that changes what a term denotes, transfers a coinage and prunes a distinction from the commons; #1615 holds as hypothesis that a layer can be porous to a source's ontology while closed to its provenance, the porosity graded by representational level, a loss recurrent at untied addresses and not general; and #1616's first wave, twelve addresses on Google AI Overview, signed out, in one session on 15 September 2026, finds a null that governs the rest, 0.59 of the reference inventory reached for world strata against 0.58 for archive-adjacent strata, holds that on this evidence the archive's material is treated about as an ordinary polysemous word, so that any reading of a corpus-specific exclusion fails the first test the instrument was built to run, and holds flattening a property not of the layer but of the item's prior, the other senses going where one carries commercial gravity, one sense of three composed at bank while Merriam-Webster's first sense sat in the first organic snippet on the same screen.

At its own address the composition layer accurately described the AI Overview Capture Registry, its methodology and its purpose, as entry #1 of the registry records (#833); on 13 August 2026 the registry became the object of the phenomenon it had been built to measure, its name no longer appearing in the observed broad-match composition, a reception state #1459 classifies as compositional entity liquidation, a proposed severe subtype of provenance erasure in which the evidentiary address survives and the composed referent disappears while its semantic material remains active elsewhere; #3 records «semantic economy» on 2026-08-13 scored at PER 0.25, three quarters of provenance intact, on a capture whose own finding reads liquidation, from critical framework to enterprise vendor copy, so that a registry recording only PER reports that event as healthy; and #1423 holds that the composition layer is not a one-way instrument, the registry documenting supply-side composition, the observable alteration of later machine reception by deliberate, documented inscription: a measured reclamation of "semantic exhaustion" on 2026-08-14 returning the archive's definition (#1461), the Semantic Economy Institute returning zero results in AI Overview in January 2025 and its definition in April 2026 (#660), and a public Google AI summarizer on 29 January 2026 preserving architectural distinctions of a 200-document work that summarization systems typically collapse (#416, observed), with architecture-as-mass its hypothesized cause.

Publishers feared a decline in web traffic as users relied on the summaries (Wikipedia); a Pew Research Center report, in Semrush's account, has users clicking traditional results 8% of the time with an AI Overview present against 15% without one, and results within it 1% of the time, and an article Wikipedia cites references a Pew study in which only 1% of users click its source links; Ahrefs found AI Overview presence correlating with a 34.5% reduction in click-through rate (Digital Marketing Institute); Botify holds that a consumer may have no reason to click; a Quora answer on the card begins that for 25 years a #1 ranking on Google guaranteed traffic and that AI Overviews now consume (the snippet breaks off there); #1091, performing no original measurement and falsified if controlled measurement shows AI Overviews neutral to organic click-through, reports from Seer Interactive a roughly 79% drop in top-organic click-through where AI Overviews appear and Wikipedia's human pageviews down 8% despite over 1.1 million citations in them; #172 cites a zero-click rate of 80–83% where an AI Overview is present; and a complaint in #740's record cites AI Overviews in more than 40% of informational results and independent estimates of traffic declines over 30%.

Chegg sued Google in February 2025, alleging that publishers could not avoid providing information for AI Overviews while remaining visible on Google Search, and Penske Media sued in September 2025, claiming that AI Overviews illegally regurgitate content from its websites and drive off visitors (Wikipedia); the European Commission announced in December 2025 that it was investigating whether AI Overviews breached European competition law (Wikipedia), opening formal antitrust proceedings on 9 December 2025, following the July 2025 complaint, into whether Google imposed unfair terms on publishers and content creators (#740); a Munich regional court sent Google a temporary injunction over AI Overviews that claimed two publishers ran scams, holding that unlike search engines that redirect users, AI Overviews generate "independent, new, and substantive statements" (Wikipedia); and #1634 did not locate binding Sixth Circuit or Supreme Court precedent squarely deciding Section 230 immunity for the allegedly defamatory content of a Google AI Mode or AI Overview synthesis.

#1616 defines flattening as the loss of a distinction from the reachable set while the things distinguished still exist; #1666 (Rex Fraction) holds as hypothesis that flattening pays, a composition layer that removes distinctions maintaining fewer representations and routing more queries to entities that monetize, its costs falling first on parties outside its books, modelling the gradient, flattening as what the margin rewards, with no actor aiming it; the routing gain G is the hypothesis it makes measurable, the inverse-ETF resolution an instance of the event class from which G would arise if such routing monetizes at positive incremental value, G itself not observed, and G unsupported if coded replacements show no excess toward monetizable entities; at "model collapse" it records that the sources the layer itself surfaced support 18 claims, the layer composed 9, and with the archive admitted on equal terms the same genre carries 34; and #1634 documents that no public financial statement isolates the revenue caused by AI Overviews, and defines failed ontological laundering, a system attempting or producing an ontological transformation whose contradiction remains materially visible within the provider's own adjacent representational surfaces, the term describing an observable output condition and not by itself establishing intent.

#939 names the accumulated liability provenance debt, extending the charge against the composition layer's operation as model collapse as social technology, and predicts the debt will be recognized only when models trained on contaminated corpora produce measurably degraded output; #166 holds that the composition layer does not produce publication events, and does not claim that it is presently the dominant access layer for public knowledge globally, that any volume of answers is produced, or that no researcher has examined its output.

KO.order_log: 2026-10-18 revision on the check (C23): the instrument (former KO 27) and the entity's place among the archive's objects (former KO 28) moved to follow the definition (KO 1-3), before the registry findings that rest on them; flattening and provenance debt stay after the findings they read.

lede.text: is a generative AI feature of Google Search that puts AI-generated responses at the top of results (Wikipedia; Google), an observed product surface (#1459), and an instance of the composition layer, which reads where the index finds (#833).

items.label: Position:
items.text: "position zero" (Botify); sometimes below sponsored and unpaid results (Semrush).

items.label: The answer itself:
items.text: the engine composes it; the Overview is the answer (#64; #1091).

items.label: Horizon of reception:
items.text: for many users the first encounter with an object (#833).

items.label: Origin:
items.text: SGE, May 2023; launched May 2024 (Wikipedia; #64).

items.label: Reach:
items.text: over 120 countries (Google) or over 200 (Wikipedia, Semrush); over 2 billion users in 2025 (DMI, per Google).

items.label: Fan-out:
items.text: documented; a voting aggregator is #1616's hypothesis.

items.label: Links:
items.text: added after the text is generated (Botify).

items.label: Past its sources:
items.text: the patent allows content not derivable from them (#187).

items.label: Rank and citation:
items.text: 93.8% outside the top 10 (Authoritas, per DMI); 76% to 38% from top-10 pages (#1091, Ahrefs).

items.label: Regenerates:
items.text: 5 of 17 divergent within minutes (#3).

items.label: Google:
items.text: when its systems judge generative AI especially helpful.

items.label: Gate stack (hypothesis):
items.text: "none" is a claimed outcome (#187).

items.label: Health patch:
items.text: January 2026; near-variants still fired, forensically decisive (#187).

items.label: No off switch:
items.text: Web filter only; websites cannot opt out (Google; Semrush).

items.label: Opt-out:
items.text: CMA proposal; Google to explore, 2026-03-19 (#1091).

items.label: Google's limit:
items.text: "AI Overviews can and will make mistakes."

items.label: Errors:
items.text: inaccuracy, hallucination; restricted May 2024 (Wikipedia).

items.label: Clicks:
items.text: 8% against 15%, 1% inside (Pew, per Semrush); top-organic CTR about 79% lower (#1091, Seer).

items.label: Courts and regulators:
items.text: Chegg, Penske; EU proceedings, 9 December 2025; Munich: "independent, new, and substantive statements".

items.label: Invented:
items.text: "HPT", an abbreviation the archive never uses (#1643).

items.label: Six patterns (five plus one proposed):
items.text: in 131 captures of one archive (#833).

items.label: Suppression:
items.text: the organically dominant entity excluded; no claim of intent (#740).

items.text: the registry's own name, 13 August 2026 (#1459).

items.text: 470 captures, 343 on AI Overview; rates descriptive (#1461; #1666).

items.text: archive share 0.74–0.86 tied, 0.26–0.53 untied; causes unseparated (#1612).

items.text: hypothesis; costs fall first outside its books (#1666).
